statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is the maximum path sum of root. The maximum path sum is defined as follows: a non-empty simple path is a finite sequence p_0,...,p_k with k >= 0 of pairwise distinct nodes of root such that for every i with 0 <= i < k, p_i and p_{i+1} are a parent and a child in root in either order; its sum is val(p_0)+...+val(p_k), where val(n) is the integer stored at node n. The maximum is taken over all such non-empty simple paths in root. Single-node paths are allowed, paths need not pass through the designated root, and empty paths are not allowed.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree (Tree) with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: For every such root, the function returns a result (a successful Result carrying an i64); it never fails by overflow, by panic, by an out-of-bounds access, or by returning an error.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a non-empty simple path P in root whose node-value sum is r. Here a simple path is a finite sequence p_0,...,p_k with k >= 0 of pairwise distinct nodes of root such that for every i with 0 <= i < k, p_i and p_{i+1} are a parent and a child in root in either order; its node-value sum is val(p_0)+...+val(p_k).
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every non-empty simple path P in root, the sum of val(n) over all nodes n on P is at most r. Here a simple path is a finite sequence p_0,...,p_k with k >= 0 of pairwise distinct nodes of root such that for every i with 0 <= i < k, p_i and p_{i+1} are a parent and a child in root in either order.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the sum of val(n) over all nodes n of root whose value is positive (this sum is 0 if root has no positive-valued node).
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000].

statement: The function returns a result r and r = v.
preconditions: root is exactly Node(v, Null, Null) for some integer v with -1000 <= v <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(a, b, a+b), where max is the maximum of the three mathematical integers.
preconditions: root is either Node(a, Node(b, Null, Null), Null) or Node(a, Null, Node(b, Null, Null)), where -1000 <= a <= 1000 and -1000 <= b <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(a, b, c, a+b, a+c, a+b+c), where max is over the six listed mathematical integers.
preconditions: root is exactly Node(a, Node(b, Null, Null), Node(c, Null, Null)) for integers a,b,c in [-1000, 1000].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the maximum of val(n) over all nodes n of root.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, every node value is in [-1000, 1000], and every node value is at most 0.

statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the sum of val(n) over all nodes n of root.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, every node value is in [-1000, 1000], every node value is at least 0, and root is a chain: every node has at most one non-Null child.

statement: Whenever max_path_sum(root) returns a result r and max_path_sum(mirror(root)) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and every node value is an integer in [-1000, 1000]. Define mirror(root) recursively by mirror(Null) = Null and mirror(Node(v,l,r)) = Node(v,mirror(r),mirror(l)).

statement: Whenever max_path_sum(root) returns a result r and max_path_sum(root') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, every node value is in [-1000, 1000], and root' is any tree obtained from root by choosing one node u of root and swapping its left and right subtrees, with all other nodes and edges unchanged.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(a, b, c, a+b, b+c, a+b+c), where max is over the six listed mathematical integers.
preconditions: root is a chain with exactly three nodes, and a,b,c are its node values in top-to-bottom order, with -1000 <= a <= 1000, -1000 <= b <= 1000, and -1000 <= c <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = c * L, where L is the maximum number of nodes in a non-empty simple path in root. Here a simple path is a finite sequence p_0,...,p_k with k >= 0 of pairwise distinct nodes of root such that consecutive nodes are parent and child in either order.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, and there is an integer c with 1 <= c <= 1000 such that every node value equals c.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max_{1 <= i <= j <= n} (a_i + ... + a_j), the maximum over all non-empty contiguous segments of the chain, computed as mathematical integers.
preconditions: root is a finite binary tree with at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, every node value is in [-1000, 1000], and root is a chain. Let a_1,...,a_n be the node values in top-to-bottom order (n >= 1).

statement: Whenever max_path_sum(root) returns a result r and max_path_sum(root') returns a result r', we have r <= r'.
preconditions: root and root' are finite binary trees with the same shape (the same Null/Node structure), each has at least one node and at most 30000 nodes, every node value in both trees is in [-1000, 1000], and for every node n of root with corresponding node n' of root', val(n) <= val(n').
